desc_letters.message: Each letter has a most common basic sound. Mastering these 26 sounds is the first step in phonics.

tip_letters.message: There are 5 vowels: A E I O U, the rest are consonants.

desc_short_vowels.message: Consonant + Vowel + Consonant (CVC structure), the vowel in the middle makes a "short sound". Short sounds are the most basic and common vowel sounds.

tip_short_vowels.message: Short sounds are crisp and short, like /æ/ in cat, /ɒ/ in dog.

desc_long_vowels.message: Long vowels are when the vowel letter "says its own name". There are two ways to make a vowel long: Magic-E and Vowel Teams.

tip_long_vowels.message: A says /eɪ/, E says /iː/, I says /aɪ/, O says /oʊ/, U says /juː/.

desc_consonant_blends.message: Two consonant letters combined to make a new, independent sound (Digraphs). Note: This is not two sounds blended, but a new sound.

tip_consonant_blends.message: sh, ch, th, ng each make a unique sound and need to be memorized separately.

desc_r_controlled.message: When a vowel is followed by the letter r, the r "bossily" changes the vowel's sound to create a unique sound.

tip_r_controlled.message: er, ir, ur all sound exactly the same: /ɜːr/.

desc_other_vowels.message: Some special vowel combinations that make "diphthongs" - the mouth shape changes noticeably during pronunciation.

rule_magic_e_a.message: Magic-E: The e at the end is silent but makes the a say its long sound /eɪ/ (letter A's name).

rule_magic_e_i.message: Magic-E: The e at the end makes the i say its long sound /aɪ/ (letter I's name).

rule_magic_e_o.message: Magic-E: The e at the end makes the o say its long sound /oʊ/ (letter O's name).

rule_magic_e_u.message: Magic-E: The e at the end makes the u say its long sound /juː/ (letter U's name).

rule_vowel_team_ai.message: Vowel Team: Two vowels together, the first one says its long sound, the second is silent.

rule_vowel_team_ay.message: Vowel Team: ay and ai sound the same, ay usually appears at the end of a word.

rule_vowel_team_ee.message: Double Vowel Team: Two e's together say letter E's name /iː/.

rule_vowel_team_ea.message: Vowel Team: ea usually says /iː/, e speaks, a is silent.

rule_vowel_team_oa.message: Vowel Team: o says long sound /oʊ/, a is silent.

rule_vowel_team_ow_long.message: ow has two sounds: /oʊ/ (like snow) or /aʊ/ (like cow). Here it is /oʊ/.

rule_vowel_team_igh.message: Special Combo: Only i speaks in igh, gh is completely silent.

rule_vowel_team_oo.message: Double O: Usually says long sound /uː/, but sometimes short /ʊ/.

rule_blend_sh.message: Digraph: sh makes a new sound, like the "shh" sound to quiet someone.

rule_blend_ch.message: Digraph: ch makes a sound like a sneeze/choo-choo train, a single sound.

rule_blend_th.message: Digraph: Tongue placed between teeth to blow air.

rule_blend_ng.message: Digraph: Nasal sound, air comes out through the nose.

rule_blend_nk.message: Digraph: ng + k, nasal sound first then /k/.

rule_r_ar.message: Bossy R: r makes the a say an open-mouthed curled-tongue sound.

rule_r_ir.message: Bossy R: er, ir, ur sound exactly the same.

rule_r_ur.message: Bossy R: ur sounds the same as er, ir.

rule_r_or.message: Bossy R: or makes a round-mouthed curled-tongue sound.

rule_r_er.message: Bossy R: er makes a weakened /ər/ sound in unstressed syllables.

rule_other_ou.message: Diphthong: Mouth opens wide, sliding from "ah" to "oo".

rule_other_ow.message: Diphthong: ow says /aʊ/ here (same as ou).

rule_other_oy.message: Diphthong: oy and oi sound the same, usually at the end of a word.

rule_other_aw.message: Vowel Team: Mouth opens round, making the "aw" sound.

rule_other_au.message: Vowel Team: au and aw sound the same.
